evidence: GenExam: 1,000 samples, 10 subjects; GPT-Image-1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Image score <15% strict; most models near 0%
rationale: Descriptive benchmark title. Results reported concretely, but the closing claim of insights on the path to general AGI extends far beyond a text-to-image exam benchmark.

evidence: Theorems: bilinear zero-sum games optimal method = Hamiltonian minimization; explicit method for normal matrices; provable speed-up for disk eigenvalues; mismatch benchmarks
rationale: Title names the topic; 'acceleration' is a technical term. Abstract frames work as a first step and keeps claims within stated game and matrix classes.

evidence: Proof AUL unbiased in PU learning; 9 datasets: AUL estimation error 1/6 of AUC; vs SOTA AUC-optimization: lower cost, up to 10% better
rationale: Comparative title backed by an unbiasedness proof and a 9-dataset comparison against AUC estimation and optimization; 'up to 10%' is properly bounded.

evidence: PHIER evaluated in CALVIN and BEHAVIOR; outperforms existing methods in few-shot OOD state classification; sim-to-real zero/few-shot transfer
rationale: Explicit claim supported by two named robotic environments plus sim-to-real; no ablation isolating hierarchies is reported, but system-level evidence fits the title.

evidence: Minimax lower bound: any algorithm needs poly(1/ε) training domains for ε excess error; DomainBed: OOD accuracy rises monotonically with number of domains
rationale: A worst-case lower bound plus a monotonic trend do not establish that observed DG failures are caused by too few domains; title and abstract both assert causation.

evidence: MSTAR benchmark; HyperReal beats DCN and matches SurReal using 3% and 40% of their parameters
rationale: Name-plus-purpose title. Leaner-model and better-generalization claims are backed by the MSTAR parameter comparison against DCN and SurReal.

evidence: WT-AWP regularization of GNNs; improved natural and robust generalization across many unnamed graph tasks and models; vanishing-gradient analysis of AWP
rationale: Improvement claim matches reported multi-task results, though unnamed, unquantified and for the WT-AWP variant; absence of numbers alone is not overreach.

evidence: Tree-to-tree program translation and sequence-to-tree semantic parsing; superior to vanilla transformer on several tasks
rationale: 'Novel' is an evaluative attribute; the abstract describes a new tree encoding and scoped gains over the vanilla transformer, so title and abstract stay matched.

evidence: 20 LLMs, three MCQ benchmarks; selection bias traced to option-ID token bias; PriDe debiasing via permutation-estimated prior
rationale: Generic claim about LLMs is backed by evaluating 20 models on three benchmarks; abstract claims, including the token-bias cause, stay within the reported analyses.

evidence: Isometric within-class regularization; improved adversarial robustness on MNIST only
rationale: General title, plus claims about robust inferences 'about the world' and hierarchical manipulation, rest on a single MNIST adversarial-robustness result.

evidence: LSTM representations transferred to small-data forecasting; M3 and other datasets; outperforms majority of best time-series methods
rationale: 'Universal' forecaster and 'diverse set of time series' exceed M3-plus-others evidence where it beats only the majority of methods; sweeping 'first time' priority claim.

evidence: Post-hoc correction on model outputs; bias localized to classification layer; unspecified empirical verification of average and worst-case gains
rationale: Question title is tentative; abstract hedges ('in certain settings', 'may') and its conclusion stays within the post-hoc correction findings.

evidence: Generator-Defender adversarial training with IRGAN-style loss; claimed improved resilience vs unspecified static defenses; no datasets, models or numbers
rationale: 'Robust' rests on one unspecified comparison with static defenses; 'establishing a critical foundation for securing' automated academic evaluation generalizes far beyond reported evidence.

evidence: Theorem: optimal adversary exists for fixed policy (SA-MDP); learned attack stronger than prior; ATLA SOTA on few continuous-control environments; LSTM policies
rationale: 'Robust' and 'Optimal' attributes are backed by the optimal-adversary result and SOTA under strong adversaries; evaluation is openly scoped to a few control environments.

evidence: Mixture-of-experts data selection from a dataserver; SOTA on several unnamed target datasets for classification, detection, instance segmentation
rationale: Question title is tentative; SOTA claims are limited to 'several target datasets' and named tasks; 'optimally select' is framed as an aim.

evidence: ATOM outlier mining; CIFAR-10 in-distribution: FPR95 reduced up to 57.99% under adversarial OOD; classic and adversarial OOD tasks
rationale: Title supported by the outlier-mining analysis and gains. SOTA 'under a broad family' of OOD tasks is claimed, but only CIFAR-10 is reported.

evidence: Six zero-shot benchmarks (object, intent, fine-grained entity typing); +1.7 over task-specific SOTA, +5.3 over general method; ablation +2.8
rationale: Descriptive title. SOTA and 'general-purpose' claims are backed by six benchmarks across three task types with quantified margins.

evidence: Average 7.8x speedup vs DyGLib across multiple models, datasets, tasks; 175x faster discretization; demos of dynamic property prediction
rationale: 'Efficient' supported by quantified speedups; 'first to unify CTDG and DTDG' is a qualified priority claim; new research uses are shown experimentally.

evidence: Constructed distribution: orthogonal-equivariant algorithms need Ω(d²) samples vs O(1) for CNNs; O(1) vs Ω(d²/ε) target-function gap; ℓ2, Adam, AdaGrad
rationale: Question title; abstract proves a sample-complexity separation and identifies equivariance as the mechanism, with assumptions stated.

evidence: Unspecified empirical study: improves accuracy over current SOTA sampling, reduces redundancy error; pruning visualization
rationale: Name title. Hedged ('could augment') improvement claim; no datasets or numbers are reported, but absence of numbers alone is not overreach.

evidence: Privacy-loss vs accuracy characterization over local NN topology for CNN image classification; PrivyNet demonstrated on CIFAR-10
rationale: 'Flexible' and 'privacy-preserving' are design attributes; effectiveness is scoped to CIFAR-10 in the abstract. Torn with mild given the general 'DNN training' framing.

evidence: Curriculum over environment settings; on par with best exhaustive grid-search policies at lower compute; unnamed tasks
rationale: Purpose phrase 'to Improve' is tentative; observations are scoped to 'each task we considered' and parity with grid search is reported.

evidence: Theory and simulations: preset polarities speed learning; image classification: polarity transfers better than weights; cases where presetting is disadvantageous
rationale: 'All you need' sufficiency is contradicted by the abstract's own disadvantageous cases; abstract also asserts a biological 'why' and value for NI from ANN simulations.

evidence: Unspecified experiments: CoCon incorporates target content and controls high-level attributes zero-shot
rationale: Name-plus-description title. Modest 'can' claims about content control; no benchmarks named, but absence of numbers is not overreach.

evidence: DAGGER-trained imitation policy over AL heuristics; well-known unnamed datasets; outperforms SOTA imitation learners and heuristics
rationale: Name title. Outperformance claim refers to the reported (unnamed) dataset experiments; no broader claims are made.

evidence: ResNets on CIFAR10 and ImageNet; tickets emerge at weight-magnitude saturation; ResNet50 75.02% top-1 at 80% pruning in 22% of epochs
rationale: Slogan 'the sooner the better' is unqualified, while the abstract reports that pruning before saturation degrades accuracy; abstract claims are backed by named experiments.

evidence: Batch size varied up to full batch; Adam gains with larger batches, SGD less; large-batch Adam resembles sign descent with momentum
rationale: Negative title claim matches full-batch evidence; the sign-descent clause is hedged ('might'), matching the reported similarity.

evidence: Function-approximation analysis of NeRF and GS; PH-Dropout on pre-trained NeRF/GS models; unspecified 'extensive evaluations'
rationale: 'Practical' fits training-free use on pre-trained models. 'First real-time and accurate' is qualified; evaluation unspecified, but absence of numbers is not overreach.

evidence: RUBICON on TD3 and TD3+BC; building-RL environments, multiple tasks and weather; +40.7% offline, +49.7% online reward
rationale: Descriptive title. Quantified gains over representative baselines in building-control environments; claims stay within the evidence.

evidence: Transformers succeed on sparse parity/majority (LSTMs fail); fail on random k-juntas; sensitivity analysis; simplicity-trap experiment; sensitivity-penalty loss escapes
rationale: Implicit simplicity-bias claim is tested. Concluding 'particularly ineffective for learning boolean functions' contradicts the reported successes on parity and majority.

evidence: GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, MultiArith; larger-model guidance +24 on GSM8K for 7B; QuestCoT gains +5 to +9 across smaller models
rationale: Implicit claim that the first step matters is supported by guided-start and QuestCoT gains on four named datasets; 'all models' refers to tested ones.

evidence: Paired structured/semi-structured tables; diagnostic splits; SQL-based, LLM and hybrid methods compared; trade-offs grow with table size, query complexity
rationale: Descriptive title. 'First controlled study' is narrowly qualified; findings and recommendations follow the reported comparisons.

evidence: BadVLMDriver on two VLMs, five physical triggers, two malicious behaviors; 92% attack success for sudden acceleration with red balloon
rationale: 'Can jeopardize' is a possibility claim backed by 92% attack success. Abstract escalates to a significant real-world threat to vehicle safety from two VLMs.

evidence: Standard ZSDA benchmarks (unnamed) and an in-house surgical dataset with smoke, blood, low lighting
rationale: Descriptive method title. Effectiveness and generalization claims are modest and tied to the stated benchmarks and surgical dataset.

evidence: LLaMA 3.2 1B; unlearning seven Harry Potter novels; unlearning metrics improve but PII regurgitation increases, amplified under red-teaming
rationale: Title is scoped to one model and matches findings. Abstract asserts a mechanism (shift toward memorized remnants in adjacent data) without reported evidence.

evidence: Range of GANs; matching subnetworks at 67-74% sparsity; discriminator initialization matters; transfer; beats prior GAN compression on SNGAN, CycleGAN
rationale: Existence claim directly supported across a range of GANs; 'first time' is qualified to GANs; outperformance shown on named models.

evidence: CGE and RGL eviction strategies; outperforms full KV cache on long-text tasks using 50% cache; no models or benchmarks named
rationale: 'Big difference' loosely matches beating full KV at 50% cache. 'Integrates seamlessly with existing LLMs' and 'consistently outperforms' lack any named models or tasks.

evidence: NARF on synthetic and large real-world datasets, implemented with two representative CDR algorithms; outperforms baselines; observation that CDR methods struggle
rationale: Topic title. Outperformance claims are tied to reported experiments; unquantified 'significantly' is not overreach under the rules.

evidence: Simulation and real robots; modalities, physics parameters, morphologies; aligns real-arm monocular video to simulated arm; policy transfer without fine-tuning
rationale: Gerund 'Learning' title. Claims about unpaired correspondence and policy transfer are matched by described simulation and real-robot experiments.

evidence: Proofs in nonparametric binary classification: minimax-optimal undersampling always exists under label shift; under group-covariate shift only with small overlap; one label-shift experiment
rationale: Optimality title is theorem-backed for label shift but drops the binary and small-overlap conditions for group shift; the abstract states assumptions carefully.

evidence: BERT classifier on Korean postpositions -ey, -eyse, -(u)lo; accuracy inversely related to function count; corpus size effects; gains over epochs
rationale: Question title is matched by the classification analyses. Claim that BERT 'simulates human interpretation' has no reported human comparison.

evidence: CamVid and Cityscapes; 20+ fps on 960x720; ~6x over single-frame baseline, 2.5x over fastest prior work; competitive accuracy
rationale: 'Fast' attribute directly supported by quantified speedups and frame rates on two named datasets.

evidence: STAMP vs recent pruning methods on unnamed benchmark datasets; better compression at similar accuracy; orders-of-magnitude faster training
rationale: 'Rapid' matches reported faster training. Claim that the mask generator generalizes 'to any unseen datasets' exceeds the unnamed benchmark evaluation.

evidence: Multiple mask-based methods (e.g., medical images with expert masks); generalization improves under covariate shift; weak link between attribution correction and generalization
rationale: Hedged title ('Possible') matches the finding of no strong correspondence; abstract conclusions are hedged ('suggest', 'may not always').

evidence: MMD string-kernel test: median 77.4% power, ~10 samples per prompt; audit of four Llama models: 11 of 31 endpoints differ
rationale: Question title answered by quantified test power and an API audit; claims stay within reported results.

evidence: SpurLens with GPT-4 and open-set detectors; various unnamed MLLMs/datasets; cue removal lowers accuracy; >10x hallucination amplification; robustness checks
rationale: Name-plus-description title. Failure-mode causal claims are backed by cue-removal interventions and robustness checks.

evidence: Encoder with proximity constraint on co-browsed product pairs; transfer-learning effectiveness comparable to several industrial baselines
rationale: Title and abstract claim the constraint improves representations, but the only reported result is parity with industrial baselines; the regularization effect's outcome is unreported.

evidence: Formal proofs: MaxEnt RL solves a class of POMDPs; equivalent to two-player game with adversarial reward
rationale: Question title; theorem claims are scoped to 'certain classes' and implications are hedged ('suggest', 'may').

evidence: PENS (ALiBi/RoPE adapted) with coordinate rescaling; trained on TSP-100; state-of-the-art up to 10,000-city Euclidean TSP
rationale: 'Solving the TSP' claims a solution; evidence is relative SOTA on Euclidean instances. Conclusion generalizes to neural combinatorial optimization from TSP alone.

evidence: CAM encoder with attention mining loss; state-of-the-art on several unnamed datasets; ablations
rationale: Bare-verb 'improve' read as a tentative outcome claim (torn with 2); SOTA on several datasets supports the improvement.
